groups.name: Liberal democratic
groups.description: Pluralist parties centred on individual rights, market economics and constitutional limits on power.

groups.name: Social democratic / left
groups.description: Parties of the democratic left: welfare states, labour rights and regulated markets.

groups.name: Conservative / centre-right
groups.description: Centre-right parties emphasising tradition, markets, order and national institutions.

groups.name: Nationalist / populist right
groups.description: Parties prioritising national sovereignty, identity and restrictive immigration, often anti-establishment.

groups.name: Socialist / communist
groups.description: Parties seeking public ownership of the economy, from reformed communists to Marxist-Leninist ruling parties.

groups.name: Autocratic / state-capitalist
groups.description: Systems where power is concentrated in a ruler, military, royal family or dominant party with limited competition.

groups.name: Religious / theocratic
groups.description: Movements and systems that root law and politics in religious tradition, from democratic religious parties to theocracy.

groups.name: Non-aligned / technocratic
groups.description: Technocrats, independents, regionalists and big-tent movements without a fixed ideological camp.

groups.name: Fascist / ultranationalist authoritarian
groups.description: Ultranationalist movements seeking an authoritarian state built on the nation, hostile to liberal democracy, communism and pluralism. In 2000-2026 such parties were fringe; a country turns this way only on an alternative focus path, and only with a real party of this kind.
